Rahul Gandhi’s reply to Elon Musk’s tweet today exposes two things that define Rahul Gandhi’s and the Congress ecosystem’s politics. Nothing exposes them better than this one tweet.

First, when discussions were going on last year about Starlink’s possible entry into India, the Congress party opposed it, alleging that this was being done to support businessmen close to Prime Minister Modi. They even brought in the national security angle to oppose Starlink’s entry.

And now, the same Rahul Gandhi has made a complete U-turn and is pushing for Starlink’s entry into India. He has not only reversed his party’s stand from a few months ago, but has also conveniently forgotten the national security arguments his own party had raised then.

This shows that Rahul Gandhi’s opposition is simply for the sake of opposition. When they thought the Modi government was supporting Starlink, they opposed it. Now, when they think the government is opposing it, they are supporting Starlink.

They can sway whichever way they want, as long as it is to oppose Modi. Principles, consistency and even national security can be conveniently forgotten.

Second, look at what has happened today and how history has parallels to this.

Rahul Gandhi is supporting a foreign businessman because he believes Indian businessmen are close to the Prime Minister. He seems willing to welcome a foreign businessman to challenge Indian businesses simply because he believes those businesses support Modi.

This reminds us of Jaichand. There are many such examples in Indian history where our own people sided with foreign interests to further their individual political ambitions. Every time, such choices cost the nation dearly. These divisions and betrayals contributed to centuries of foreign domination and subjugation.

Rahul Gandhi seems determined to replay the same textbook.

But this time, the consequences could extend beyond political hegemony to technological and economic dependence as well.

And for what? Just to oppose Modi?

Will you oppose India just to oppose Modi, Mr. Rahul Gandhi?

It is unfortunate that we have a Leader of Opposition like you, Mr. Rahul Gandhi.

note_tweet.text:
In 1993, this photo of Belgian soldiers holding a Somali boy over an open fire shocked the world.

The soldiers were in Mogadishu as part of the UN-authorized Operation Restore Hope, supposedly there to protect Somalis and deliver humanitarian assistance.

The photograph became evidence in a military prosecution.

And what happened next was even more shocking.

In June 1997, a Belgian military court acquitted the two soldiers, Claude Baert and Kurt Coelus, of assault, battery and threats.

Their defence?

They claimed it was merely a “game.”

The court accepted that there was insufficient evidence that the boy had suffered bodily harm or that his life had been threatened.

The prosecution appealed.

In December 1997, the acquittal was confirmed.

Imagine being the Somali child in that photograph.

Imagine watching the men who held you over a fire walk free because a court decided there was insufficient proof that you had been harmed.

This is part of the history that disappears when Western military interventions in Africa are remembered only through the language of “peacekeeping” and “humanitarianism.”
